edits.content: For each flight leg, require a `departure_date` and at least one starting-airport identifier: `start_airport_city`, `start_airport`, or `start_airport_code`. Treat this conditional origin requirement as mandatory even though each field is individually optional; ask for any missing required detail before searching.

- Use exact supported field names when mapping criteria: hotel hot tubs and saunas map to `has_hot_tub=True` and `has_sauna=True`; a nightshade-allergy accommodation request maps to the supported restaurant field `has_tomato_allergy_options=True`. For a guest-rating floor, use `[N, 5]`; reserve equal bounds for explicitly exact ratings or categories.

edits.target: - Pass only criteria supported by the conversation, map each value to the field that expresses it, and preserve the user's entity text. For example, put a state abbreviation in `state`, not `city`. Use the tool's accepted format for preferences such as time ranges; use an example format only when supported by the tool. Distinguish hotel stars (`stars`) from guest ratings (`rating`); for a supported “at least N stars” constraint, use the inclusive range from N to the field's maximum, and for an exact category use the same value as both bounds. Do not add unrelated preferences.
edits.content: - Pass only criteria supported by the conversation, map each value to the field that expresses it, and preserve the user's entity text. For example, put a state abbreviation in `state`, not `city`. Check argument types against the tool schema: a single airport name or code is a scalar string (for example, `end_airport="ANC"`), not a one-item list. Use the tool's accepted format for preferences such as time ranges; use an example format only when supported by the tool. Distinguish hotel stars (`stars`) from guest ratings (`rating`): for “at least N stars,” use the inclusive range from N to the field's maximum; for an exact category, use equal bounds. For flight-time constraints, use the format accepted by the flight tool, such as 12-hour AM/PM strings. Do not copy a time verbatim from a cache summary if it is displayed in a different format; express an exact-time request with identical range endpoints and an “arrive by” request as a range from midnight to the stated time. Do not add unrelated preferences.

edits.target: - When the user requests proximity, use the relevant hotel and attraction or restaurant results with `search_nearest`. Set `groupBy` to the domain the user wants prioritized.
edits.content: - Treat a request to stay “in” or “near” a named neighborhood or district as a hotel `neighborhood` constraint, not a `search_nearest` request. Do not use `search_nearest` as a substitute for an on-site hotel feature or amenity. Use it when the user wants proximity between two distinct domains (hotels, attractions, or restaurants): provide exactly two compatible result objects, one for each domain, and ensure one includes any named target (run a focused exact-name search if needed). For hotels near attractions, search for both hotels and the requested attraction category, then set `groupBy` to hotels. In other cases, set `groupBy` to the domain the user wants prioritized.
